Three opt-in filters for the OS/2 and post values FontForge's TTF exporter computes. `--fontforge-os2-defaults` and `--fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean` fill values the source does not state; `--fontforge-underline-position` converts the UnderlinePosition the source states.

- `--fontforge-underline-position`: FontForge's UnderlinePosition is the underline's centre, post.underlinePosition its top; applies `dumppost()`'s rule up to tag 20170731, position - thickness/2 in real arithmetic truncated towards zero. FontForge reversed the sign in commit 9f667c9c (fontforge/fontforge#3389, first in tag 20190317), so the flag is for a binary exported by an older FontForge, whatever the export date.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, sub/superscript and strikeout: when the source has no OS2SubXSize (FontForge's `subsuper_set`), all ten from `SFDefaultOS2SubSuper` (tottf.c), with the x offsets derived from the y offsets already truncated to 16 bits.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, PANOSE: as `SFDefaultOS2Info` computes it. `OS2WeightCheck` sets byte 2 from the Weight: name and then from the FontName; "script" in the FontName (without "sans") sets byte 0 to 3; FontName width words set byte 3, and one shared advance (`CIDOneWidth`) sets it to 9.
- `--fontforge-os2-defaults`, x-height and cap height: each one the source does not state, as `setos2` fills it from `SFXHeight`/`SFCapHeight` (`SFStandardHeight`, splinefont.c).
- `--fontforge-height-glyph-count-mean`: the x-height and cap height as a FontForge built before 2012-05-14 (commit 4d34d21ef866) computed them, the sum of the distinct round or pointed tops divided by the glyph count. Run it before `--fontforge-os2-defaults`.

Five opt-in filters for converting a FontForge source, and one CLI change.

- `--drop-alternate-unicodes`: drop the plain AltUni2 alternate codepoints and keep each glyph's Encoding codepoint, for a target cmap that does not carry the alternates. FontForge's own TTF export does map them, whatever the encoding (`NeedsUCS2Table()` in tottf.c; for a Unicode encoding, `SFD_DoAltUnis()` in sfd.c adds them to the encoding map first; the same in 20120731 and 20230101). Variation sequences are untouched; a glyph with no Encoding codepoint keeps its first one.
- `--reverse-path-direction`: reverse every closed contour; the counterpart to `--correct-path-direction` for a font whose mixed contour directions are meant to be kept.
- `--keep-source-glyph-names`: set the Glyphs custom parameter "Don't use Production Names", so a later compile keeps the glyph names the source states, as FontForge's TTF export does (`dumppost()` in tottf.c).
- `--keep-source-advances`: record an uncategorised glyph with a non-zero advance as a base, so a compiler does not zero its advance as a mark by its name. Run `--infer-mark-category` first.
- `--snap-component-transforms`: read a component scale within 1.5 F2Dot14 steps of an integer as that integer (FontForge stores a mirror as -0.999939, which `put2d14()` exports as -1), and round every component offset with rint, ties to even, as `dumpcomposite()` in tottf.c does. The scale rule is not `put2d14()`'s floor: FontForge exports +0.999939 as 16383/16384, this filter reads it as 1.
- CLI (not opt-in): when compiling a TTF, `babelfont` now honours a "Don't use Production Names" custom parameter that is enabled and set to 1, so a .glyphs source that already carries it compiles without production names. A disabled parameter, or one set to 0, changes nothing.

issues.what: pfmset is not modelled. When sf->pfminfo.pfmset is unset, SFDefaultOS2Info memsets sf->pfminfo (initTables passes &sf->pfminfo). pfmset is unset when there is no PfmFamily, TTFWeight/PfmWeight, TTFWidth, LineGap or VLineGap line (sfd.c 20170731, lines 7559-7610). FontForge then discards a stated Panose, the OS2Sub group and OS2XHeight/OS2CapHeight, and recomputes all of them. It also derives usWeightClass and usWidthClass from the same OS2WeightCheck and width chain, so Light gives 200. The filter keeps those stated values and fills no weight or width class. Only hand-edited SFDs are affected, since fontinfo.c sets pfmset whenever it sets panose_set or subsuper_set. That is the same class of case the fixer used to justify the all-ten gating.
issues.fix: Either model pfmset (the reader already parses those keys) or add one rustdoc sentence saying that sources with none of the pfmset lines are not modelled.

issues.where: babelfont/src/filters/snapcomponenttransforms.rs:44-58 (apply loop); rustdoc :10-22; help :76-81; commit 9053387; PR body bullet --snap-component-transforms
issues.what: This is not a faithful port of when FontForge uses these rules. FontForge floors the scale (put2d14) and rint's the offset only in dumpcomposite, which runs only for IsTTFRefable glyphs: the layer has references and no contours, and every 2x2 entry is in [-2, 1.999939] (tottf.c v20120731-b:1065-1078, 20230101:1030-1043). Every other glyph goes through dumpglyph/SCttfApprox. That path flattens the reference with its raw transform and applies rint to each resulting point (SSAddPoints, v20120731-b ~788-800), so the offset is never rounded on its own and -0.999939 is used as it is. The filter snaps every component in every layer, so for a glyph mixing contours and components it moves points away from FontForge's output. I confirmed this with the HEAD binary on an SFD glyph with a contour plus `Refer: 1 40 N 1 0 0 1 0.5 0 2` to a glyph with points at x=101 and x=301. Without the filter the TTF has x=102 and 302, the same as FontForge's rint(101.5)=102 and rint(301.5)=302. With --snap-component-transforms it has x=101 and 301. A fractional point with a non-tie offset diverges too: p=442.4, t=0.4 gives 443 in FontForge and 442 with the filter.
issues.fix: Apply the snap only where FontForge would write a composite: skip a layer that has any Shape::Path, and skip a component whose 2x2 matrix is outside [-2, 1.999939]. Add a test with a mixed glyph whose component offset is 0.5, and say 'for a glyph made only of components' in the rustdoc, help and PR bullet. At the least, state the scope in the rustdoc, help and PR body. Any conversion re-landed with this filter should be re-checked for mixed glyphs with fractional offsets.

issues.what: 'FontForge stores a mirror as -0.999939' is stated as a general fact, and it is not one. The FontForge SFD writer prints transforms with %g, so an exact mirror is written as -1. Its TTF importer reads 0xC000 as exactly -1 (parsettf.c get2dot14). -0.999939 appears only when a source carries -16383/16384, for example one imported from a binary that stored 0xC001. Separately, the commit subject ('round component transforms as FontForge's exporter does'), the rustdoc summary ('reads a FontForge component transform as FontForge's exporter writes it') and the help's closing 'as FontForge's exporter does' all claim exporter fidelity. The same rustdoc then says the scale rule is not put2d14's, and the issue above shows the offset rule is not applied where FontForge applies it. A maintainer who knows F2Dot14 will notice the contradiction.
issues.fix: Write 'a FontForge source may carry a mirror as -0.999939 (-16383/16384 to six digits), which put2d14 exports as -1'. Change the subject to something like 'Add a filter to snap near-integer component scales and round component offsets'. In the rustdoc summary, say what the filter does rather than 'as the exporter writes it', and keep 'as dumpcomposite does' only for the offset rule.
